# hush_cloudflare_r2_access_credential (Resource)

Manage Cloudflare R2 access credentials in the Hush Security platform. With the root API token, the access manager issues an R2 token per policy version and hands the workload its S3 credentials: `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key` and `endpoint`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a Cloudflare R2 dynamic access credential
resource "hush_cloudflare_r2_access_credential" "example" {
  name           = "prod-r2"
  description    = "Production Cloudflare R2 credential"
  deployment_ids = [hush_deployment.example.id]
  account_id     = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"

  api_token_wo         = var.cloudflare_root_api_token
  api_token_wo_version = "1"
}
```

## Requirements

**hush-am chart 0.34.1 or later** on the target deployment. On an older one
the apply fails.

**A root token.** Create an account API token in the Cloudflare dashboard,
under **Manage Account > Account API Tokens**, as a custom token with the
`Account` | `Account API Tokens` | `Edit` permission on the account that holds
the buckets. The dashboard user who creates it must be allowed to manage
account API tokens. It needs no R2 permission, yet it can create R2 tokens of
any level, so treat it like an admin key. A token limited to client IP
addresses must allow the access manager's egress address. A token with an
expiry must be replaced before then: once it expires, new versions and
revocations fail.

**Network egress** from the access manager to `api.cloudflare.com`, and from
the workloads to the S3 endpoint of the privilege's jurisdiction, both on 443.

**Token quota.** A Cloudflare account holds at most 500 account API tokens.
Each live policy version holds one, named `hush-am-r2-<id>-<version>`, so plan
for about 250 policies per account, minus the account's other tokens. Do not
edit or delete these tokens by hand.

## Changing `account_id`

A new account needs a new root token in the same apply, which the plan checks.
The API refuses the change while an access policy or a dynamic credential uses
the credential, since Hush revokes tokens with the newest root token, which
cannot reach the old account. The state keeps the old account and token, so
the same configuration applies once nothing uses the credential. To move to
another account, create a credential for it. A policy deleted just before the
change can leave its `hush-am-r2-*` tokens in the old account; delete them
there by hand.

## Changing the token

Every token sent issues new credentials to every policy that uses the
credential, so the provider sends it only when `api_token` or
`api_token_wo_version` changes. Moving from `api_token` to `api_token_wo`
sends it too, even when the value is the same.

If the apply fails while Hush syncs the new token, the state keeps it, since
Hush already holds it. A credential left in error takes a new `api_token`, or
a bumped `api_token_wo_version`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (String) The Cloudflare account ID: 32 lowercase hex characters. Changing it requires a new `api_token` (or a bumped `api_token_wo_version`)
- `deployment_ids` (List of String) List of deployment IDs that can access this credential. Currently limited to a single deployment. Changing this after creation is not supported; the credential must be deleted and recreated.
- `name` (String) The name of the Cloudflare R2 access credential

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `api_token` (String, Sensitive) The root account API token, with the `Account API Tokens` `Edit` permission on the account. The access manager creates and revokes the workloads' R2 tokens with it; it never reaches a workload. Every change issues new credentials to every policy that uses the credential
- `api_token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The root account API token (write-only). More secure than `api_token` because Terraform will not store this value in the state file.
- `api_token_wo_version` (String) Used to trigger updates for `api_token_wo`. Change when the token changes.
- `description` (String) The description of the Cloudflare R2 access credential
- `secret_store_id` (String) The ID of the secret store where this credential is saved (optional)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the Cloudflare R2 access credential
- `kind` (String) The kind of access credential
- `type` (String) The type of access credential
